skill.name: container-grype
skill.description: Guides container vulnerability scanning with Grype for images, filesystems, and SBOMs. It covers CI/CD gates, report formats, and remediation priority using CVSS, EPSS, and CISA KEV signals.
skill.summary: Scan containers and SBOMs with Grype, then prioritize CVE remediation.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, reference material, and CI syntax. Confirmed risks are limited to the bundled CI templates. They include pipe-to-shell installers, Docker socket mounting, token exposure, unquoted Tekton parameters, and an unpinned action.

remediation.issue: Remote installer scripts are piped directly into shells in CI templates.
remediation.suggestion: Download pinned release artifacts, verify checksums or signatures, and run installers as separate reviewed steps.

remediation.issue: The Jenkins example mounts the host Docker socket into a scanner container.
remediation.suggestion: Use rootless builders, remote builders, or isolated runners instead of exposing /var/run/docker.sock to job containers.

remediation.issue: The CI template passes GITHUB_TOKEN to a third-party action.
remediation.suggestion: Use least-privilege workflow permissions, pin the action to an immutable commit, and avoid token exposure when summaries are not required.

remediation.issue: The CI template uses a mutable @master action reference.
remediation.suggestion: Pin third-party actions to trusted version tags or commit SHAs and review updates through dependency management.

remediation.issue: Tekton parameters are inserted into shell commands without quoting or validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate image and severity parameters against allowlists, quote parameter expansions, or pass them as arguments to a wrapper script.

content.value_statement: Container and dependency vulnerabilities can slow releases and hide exploitable CVEs. This skill guides Grype scans, CI gates, SBOM analysis, and risk prioritization with CVSS, EPSS, and CISA KEV context.
actual_capabilities: Guides Grype scans for container images, filesystems, and SBOM files.
Explains severity thresholds for CI/CD build gates.
Prioritizes CVEs using CVSS, EPSS, and CISA KEV signals.
Documents output formats including table, JSON, SARIF, and CycloneDX.
Provides sample Grype configuration and CI pipeline templates.
limitations: Requires Grype and container tooling installed where scans run.
Does not validate runtime reachability by itself.
Scan accuracy depends on current vulnerability databases and package metadata.
CI examples need hardening before production use.

use_cases.title: Gate Container Releases
use_cases.description: Add Grype scans to builds and block releases when critical or high vulnerabilities exceed policy.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Vulnerability Backlogs
use_cases.description: Rank CVEs by exploitability, known exploitation, severity, fix availability, and production exposure.

use_cases.title: Produce Audit Evidence
use_cases.description: Create repeatable scan outputs, exception records, and remediation notes for compliance reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Scan a Container Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the container-grype skill to scan <image>. Summarize critical and high vulnerabilities, fixed versions, and immediate next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add a CI Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Grype CI step for <platform> that fails on high severity. Include artifact outputs and a short rollout plan.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Grype JSON summary: <paste summary>. Rank findings by CISA KEV, EPSS, CVSS, fix availability, and production exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Design an SBOM Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Grype workflow for <organization> using Syft SBOMs, scheduled rescans, exception handling, and audit evidence retention.

output_examples.output: A concise report lists critical and high CVEs, affected packages, fixed versions, and whether the release should continue.

output_examples.input: Assess a Grype report with many medium findings.
output_examples.output: A prioritized remediation plan separates KEV matches, high EPSS findings, fixed packages, and accepted low-risk items.

output_examples.input: Plan CI integration for GitHub Actions.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline covers the scan stage, fail threshold, SARIF upload, artifact retention, and rollback guidance.

best_practices: Pin scanner versions and verify downloaded installers before running CI templates.
Scan both build images and archived SBOMs to catch newly disclosed vulnerabilities.
Document every ignored CVE with owner, reason, expiration date, and compensating controls.
anti_patterns: Piping remote install scripts directly into a shell in production pipelines.
Treating CVSS severity as the only remediation priority.
Suppressing vulnerabilities without expiration dates or business approval.

faq.question: What does this skill scan?
faq.answer: It guides Grype scans for container images, local filesystems, and SBOM files.

faq.question: Does it install Grype automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and templates that users must review and run in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it fail a build?
faq.answer: Yes. The included workflow patterns explain Grype fail thresholds for CI/CD gates.

faq.question: How are vulnerabilities prioritized?
faq.answer: The workflow combines CVSS severity, EPSS probability, CISA KEV status, fix availability, and exposure.

faq.question: Can it reduce false positives?
faq.answer: It explains documented ignore rules, expiration dates, and review steps for accepted risk.

faq.question: Is production hardening still required?
faq.answer: Yes. CI templates should be pinned, validated, and adapted to local access controls before use.
